column3: A temple complex in Haikou for five officials of the Tang and Song dynasties who were exiled to Hainan, with halls and old trees.
A park of extinct volcano craters in Haikou, where visitors can walk to the edge of an old crater and through lava tunnels.
A long city beach in Haikou with palm trees, where locals come to swim and fly kites and watch the sun set.
A museum of Hainan's history, from the Li and Miao peoples to the island's role in the maritime Silk Road.
Poached chicken sliced and served with rice cooked in chicken stock, with ginger and chili sauce. It started in Hainan and became a classic across Southeast Asia.
A prized chicken breed from Wenchang, known for its thin skin and sweet, tender meat, and often served poached.
A plump duck from Jiaji in Qionghai, with soft meat and rich fat, usually served with a dipping sauce.
Rice noodles in a rich broth, topped with beef or pork and peanuts, an island breakfast favorite.
Sticky rice steamed inside a coconut, so the grains take up the coconut's sweet scent.
A cool dessert soup of beans, coconut milk, fruit and jelly on ice, perfect for a hot day on the island.
A Hainan teahouse custom, where people spend hours over tea, snacks and chats, and where deals and gossip are shared.
The local opera of Hainan, sung in the Hainan dialect, whose stories and melodies are loved by Hainanese all over the world.
A wide curve of white sand and clear blue water, backed by green hills and resorts, often called the most beautiful beach in Sanya.
A beach of huge boulders carved with the words for End of the Earth. In the past, exiles were sent here, at the far south of the empire.
A temple by the sea in Sanya with a 108-meter statue of Guanyin standing on the water, a pilgrimage site.
A small island off Sanya with clear water, coral reefs and white sand, popular for diving and snorkeling.
A crescent-shaped beach right beside Sanya's city center, with calm water and palm trees.
Sanya's markets let you pick live fish, crab and shellfish, and then have them cooked at a nearby restaurant.
Chicken simmered in fresh coconut water at the table, with a sweet and clean broth. It is a popular Hainan hotpot.
Sweet, golden mangoes ripen in Hainan's warm climate in spring and are sold at stalls across Sanya.
Hele crab from Wanning is one of Hainan's four famous dishes, known for rich, creamy meat and golden roe.
A cloth woven by Li women, with bold patterns of people, animals and nature. With a history of thousands of years, it is a UNESCO-listed craft.
A bay in Wanning with steady waves, a favorite for surfers, with a laid-back vibe.
A hill near Wanning with temples, rocks carved with poems and a good view of the coast.
A coffee grown in Xinglong, brought by overseas Chinese returning from Southeast Asia. It is roasted dark and often sweetened.
A town at the mouth of the Wanquan River where the Boao Forum for Asia meets, with beaches and quiet lagoons.
A clear river that flows through green hills and rubber forests and reaches the sea at Boao.
A well-known Hainan duck with soft meat and rich flavor, named for the town of Jiaji and served with a dipping sauce.
A coastal launch site, close to the equator, where China launches its large rockets and space station modules.
The old family home of the Soong family in Wenchang, whose descendants include three famous sisters of 20th-century China.
Wenchang is famous for its coconut palms, and you can drink the sweet water directly from the fruit.
A school begun by the poet Su Dongpo while he was exiled to Hainan, where he taught local students.
A thick rice porridge cooked until the grains melt, often with seafood or meat, a Danzhou comfort food.
Lychees grown on the volcanic soil of Danzhou, juicy and sweet, are picked in early summer.
Hainan's highest mountain, with five peaks like fingers, covered with rainforest and home to the Li people.
A black tea grown in the misty forests of Wuzhishan, with a clean, sweet taste.
A rice wine made by the Li people from mountain rice, often shared at festivals and family gatherings.
The Li people's biggest festival, on the third day of the third lunar month, with singing, dancing and courtship.
Ledong's mangoes are sweet and fragrant, among the first to reach markets each year.
A peninsula in Lingshui where hundreds of macaques live, which you can reach by cable car, to see them up close.
Rice noodles in a sour, spicy broth, with peanuts, herbs and fried pork skin, a Lingshui breakfast.
Lingshui's coastal restaurants serve fresh fish, crab and shrimp, often steamed or cooked with local herbs.
